newsitem.title: USA: House backs bill promoting conservation in refuges.
newsitem.headline: House backs bill promoting conservation in refuges.

text.p: The House Tuesday overwhelmingly passed a bill to promote conservation in wildlife refuges.

The legislation, backed by a vote of 407-1, originally drew loud opposition from the Clinton administration and Democrats, but was substantially revised by the House Resources Committee before going to the floor.

Republicans, led by the committee chairman Rep. Don Young of Alaska, had proposed to put fishing and hunting on a par with conservation as a purpose of the wildlife refuges. The House passed a bill with those provisions last year, but the Senate never acted on it.

The bill was reworded this year to make conservation of fish, wildlife and their habitat the mission of the refuge system and make wildlife-dependent recreation the highest priority use of refuges, as long as it was compatible with the mission of the system.

"We've built a fragile coalition between hunters and environmentalists -- good wildlife conservation means more pictures or more (animals) to shoot, depending on your game," said House Resources Committee Democratic aide.

Environmental groups hailed the bill, saying it was a sharp change from last year's legislation, which green groups feared would allow rampant recreation and ease limits on commercial development such as oil drilling in refuges.
"It establishes a clear mission statement that the refuge system basically exists to conserve fish and wildlife," said Jim Waltman, refuges and wildlife director for the Wilderness Society.
"It establishes a much more formal and public process to review which activities should be allowed in the refuges and to require comprehensive planning for the refuges," he said.
The Senate has yet to take up a similar bill.
